thread:
Rajiv Sen: Heads up — observed lots of short-lived websocket sessions in us-east-1 this morning, but clients report they never saw a close. Console shows a 2x spike in session churn and a corresponding billing delta.
Aisha Gomez: Same. Spike correlates with the rate-limiter middleware rollout at ~03:20 UTC. Looks like the proxy is tombstoning sessions aggressively when a rate-limit check returns 429 mid-stream.
Kira Park: Pulled proxy logs. Example: 
```text
[03:22:11.231] conn=abcd1234 state=active last_frame=12ms
[03:22:11.289] auth=ok rate_check=429 -> mark_tombstone conn=abcd1234 reason=quota_enforced
[03:22:11.290] ws.proxy: silent-close-detected conn=abcd1234 no_fin_seen
[03:22:11.291] session-store: create_session_tombstone id=abcd1234 ttl=0
```
Ben Ruiz: Oof. So proxy creates a tombstone immediately on rate-check fail and that causes the client reconnect to be treated as a fresh session. Double-charges if reconnection happens within seconds.
devops-bot: Alert: 7332100000 - websocket churn +180% in us-east-1 since 03:20 UTC.
Rajiv Sen: Two levers: prevent premature tombstones in the proxy, or change quota/billing to attribute reconnects to the same logical session when resume token/trace-id matches. Both ideal.
Aisha Gomez: I'm wary of adding a long grace window globally because long-lived idle sockets could hold resources. Suggest a per-route grace window and a short PING/PONG keepalive flow to detect client liveness before tombstoning.
Kira Park: Proposed proxy change: introduce ws.idle_grace_ms (default 5000) and only create tombstone after grace expiration. Also emit a debug frame when rate-limit is applied so clients can surface a clear event instead of silent drops. Example config: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: chat-stream
    ws:
      idle_grace_ms: 5000
      on_rate_limit: send_control_frame
      tombstone_immediate: false
```
Ben Ruiz: Console/telemetry problem: reconnects are logged as new sessions immediately. We need an attribution window where reconnects that present the same resume_token or trace_id within N seconds get merged for metrics and billing. Also surface a `session_lineage_id` in the session table so we can group retries.
Rajiv Sen: Agree. Console change should be additive and conservative. Add derived metric `ws.resume_credit_rate` = resumed_sessions / reconnects. Also add `tombstone_latency_hist` so we can see how quickly tombstones are created after last_frame.
Aisha Gomez: Rollout approach: 
- Proxy: canary 5% for route `chat-stream` with idle_grace_ms=5s and debug control frames enabled.
- Console: ingest resume tokens and only mark new session after 6s of no resume. Add UI toggle in billing preview to respect resume crediting for pilot tenants.
Kira Park: I'll implement proxy change. Also will add a small guard that refuses to tombstone if socket is still receiving frames within the last 2s.
Ben Ruiz: I'll own console metric + panel. Will add `session_lineage` column and create a reconciliation job to backfill last 24h. Also add a billing preview flag `respect_ws_resume` per-tenant.
Rajiv Sen: For support playbook: 
1) Check `ws.churn_rate` and recent deployments.
2) If churn coincides with middleware rollout, toggle route `tombstone_immediate=false` for the tenant.
3) Watch `ws.resume_credit_rate` and `session_lineage` panel.
Aisha Gomez: One concern: some clients legitimately drop and should be billed as new sessions. Our merge window might mask abuse. We should add heuristics: only auto-merge if resume token or trace_id cryptographically matches and the gap < 6s and client IP/ua matches.
Kira Park: Good point. We'll validate by sampling `session_lineage` traces in canary and record mismatch rate.
Ben Ruiz: Want a small histogram in the panel of time-between-last-frame-and-reconnect for merged vs new sessions. That should help tune the window.
devops-bot: Info: 7332100045 - canary started for `chat-stream` in us-east-1 (5%).
Rajiv Sen: Owners: Kira -> proxy PR, Ben -> console panels & backfill, Aisha -> policy + risk review, Rajiv -> support playbook and rollout coordination.
Aisha Gomez: Target: canary metrics in 2 hours, backfill job queued for immediate run, decision to ship wide if resume_credit_rate > 0.6 and p95 latency delta < 10ms.
Kira Park: Starting PR. I'll push a small debug flag so we can flip tombstone_immediate quickly without a full deploy.
Ben Ruiz: I'll add a temporary dashboard with `ws.churn_rate`, `ws.resume_credit_rate`, `tombstone_latency_hist`, `reconnect_ip_match_rate`.
Rajiv Sen: Thanks folks. Please post updates here as canary results come in.
